text: I count out loud. People find it irritating and I have decided not to stop.
You do not play. Then there is nothing here for me to count, and I am simply a man talking numbers to himself in a laundrette.
Which I am on most nights anyway. But I prefer an audience who can tell whether I am wrong.
A game, then. I will count the whole way through and you will find it irritating.
It is not to put you off. A game nobody counts is a game nobody learns anything from, and I have sat through a great many of those.

exit.intro: He sets his watch on the table beside the bowl and then does not look at it once.

text: Then I shall count the machines. Four of them, and the one on the end is thirty seconds behind the rest and has been all week.
Eleven. You were eleven ahead from about move forty, and you played the rest of it as though you were behind.
That is the expensive habit, and it is not reading. It is the not knowing.
Fourteen and a half. I said fourteen and a half at move sixty and it was fourteen and a half at the end.
Nobody ever believes me until the end, which is the only reason I keep doing it out loud.
